about.title: About me
about.lead: Just a regular person who likes fiddling with code and gets a real kick out of making small things that work.
about.p1: I don't build giant enterprise platforms. Most things I code start from a tiny personal annoyance — wanting to change a workout split without editing three files, or logging reps without staring at a phone screen.
about.p2: That is also why this site looks like graph paper, sticky notes, and hand-inked borders instead of a sleek sci-fi dashboard. Slightly crooked lines feel warmer and closer to how I actually sketch ideas on a desk.

habits.title: 01 · Keep it small enough to finish
habits.body: If one loop or one JSON file solves it, skip the fancy distributed plumbing.

habits.title: 02 · Keep the files on my own drive
habits.body: SQLite or plain JSON text means I can always read, diff, and back up my own data.

habits.title: 03 · Make it fun to poke at
habits.body: If a side project isn't a little bit playful, it rarely survives past the first weekend.

details.note: Grabbed an iced americano downstairs and caught this clean patch of afternoon light on the wall.
Snapped while waiting at a red light — liked how the tree shadows blended with the old brick.
Looked up after hours of coding just as a breeze lifted the corner of the curtain.
Wandered for half an hour with nowhere to be; keeping the phone pocketed lets you notice more.
Pavement still held a soft glare right after the shower stopped, stretching the streetlamp shadows.
My mug had just cooled down while sunlight sliced across one corner of the notebook.
Tucked off the main road — just a few potted plants and weathered shop signs.
Those five minutes when the sky shifts from pale blue to peach are always worth watching.
Still had chalk on my hands, sitting on the bench to cool off and snapped one.
Warm roadside lamps flicked on after dusk on a slow walk back home.

contact.p: No formal pitch needed — happy to trade notes on small side projects, playful web experiments, or a good coffee spot.
